title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 15. The Meeting with Srimad Ishvara Puri
html:
The Lord lives at home, teaching and gladdening His mother and wife; the journey to Gaya for His father's rite; a fever cured by the water from brahmanas' feet; the meeting with Ishvara Puri and initiation into the mantra

Verse 1

ततः पुरस्थैरभिनन्दितो हरि-
र्वसन्गृहे ब्राह्मणवैद्यसज्जनान्।
अपाठयल्लौकिकसत्क्रियाविधिं
चकार कारुण्यविधानमद्भुतम्॥१॥

tataḥ purasthairabhinandito hari-
rvasangṛhe brāhmaṇavaidyasajjanān|
apāṭhayallaukikasatkriyāvidhiṁ
cakāra kāruṇyavidhānamadbhutam||1||

tatah — then; pura-sthaih — by the townspeople; abhinanditah — greeted; harih — Hari; vasan — living; grihe — at home; brahmana-vaidya-sajjanan — brahmanas, vaidyas and good people; apathayat — taught; laukika-sat-kriya-vidhim — the rules of good worldly rites; chakara — observed; karunya-vidhanam — a work of mercy; adbhutam — wondrous.

1Then Hari, greeted by the townspeople, lived at home: He taught brahmanas, vaidyas1 and good people and observed the rules of good worldly rites — and this was a wondrous work of His mercy.

Verse 2

वाचस्पतेर्वाग्मितया जहार
काव्यस्य काव्येन विधोः श्रियं सः।
कान्त्या स्वयं भूमिगते सुरेशे
न्यस्तां पुनस्तां हरये ददुः किम्॥२॥

vācaspatervāgmitayā jahāra
kāvyasya kāvyena vidhoḥ śriyaṁ saḥ|
kāntyā svayaṁ bhūmigate sureśe
nyastāṁ punastāṁ haraye daduḥ kim||2||

vachaspateh — of Vachaspati (Brihaspati); vagmitaya — by eloquence; jahara — took away; kavyasya — of Kavya (Shukra); kavyena — by poetry; vidhoh — of the moon; shriyam — the splendour; sah — He; kantya — by radiance; svayam — Himself; bhumi-gate — having come to earth; sura-ishe — the Lord of the gods; nyastam — entrusted; punah — back; tam — it; haraye — to Hari; daduh — they gave; kim — did (they not)?

2By His eloquence He took away the glory of Vachaspati, by His poetry that of Kavya, by His radiance the splendour of the moon2. When the Lord of the gods Himself had come to earth, did they not give back to Hari what had been entrusted to them?

Verse 3

सोऽध्यापयद्विप्रमहत्तमांस्तान्
ये पूर्वजन्मार्जितपुण्यराशयः।
ब्रूमः कथं भाग्यवतां महद्गुणं
येषां स्वयं लोकगुरुर्गुरुर्भवेत्॥३॥

so'dhyāpayadvipramahattamāṁstān
ye pūrvajanmārjitapuṇyarāśayaḥ|
brūmaḥ kathaṁ bhāgyavatāṁ mahadguṇaṁ
yeṣāṁ svayaṁ lokagururgururbhavet||3||

sah — He; adhyapayat — taught; vipra-mahattaman — the greatest of brahmanas; tan — those; ye — who; purva-janma-arjita-punya-rashayah — had amassed heaps of merit in former births; brumah — shall we tell; katham — how; bhagyavatam — of the fortunate ones; mahat-gunam — the great merit; yesham — whose; svayam — Himself; loka-guruh — the Teacher of the world; guruh — teacher; bhavet — became.

3He taught the greatest of brahmanas — those who in former births had amassed heaps of merit. How can we describe the great merit of those fortunate ones, whose teacher the Teacher of the world Himself became?

Verse 4

सौन्दर्यमाधुर्यविलासविभ्रमै-
रराज राजद्वरहेमगौरः।
विष्णुप्रियालालितपादपङ्कजो
रसेन पूर्णो रसिकेन्द्रमौलिः॥४॥

saundaryamādhuryavilāsavibhramai-
rarāja rājadvarahemagauraḥ|
viṣṇupriyālālitapādapaṅkajo
rasena pūrṇo rasikendramauliḥ||4||

saundarya-madhurya-vilasa-vibhramaih — with beauty, sweetness, playfulness and charm; raraja — shone; rajat-vara-hema-gaurah — golden like gleaming pure gold; vishnupriya-lalita-pada-pankajah — whose lotus feet were caressed by Vishnupriya; rasena — with rasa; purnah — full; rasika-indra-maulih — the crown of the kings of rasikas.

4Gleaming like pure gold, He shone with beauty, sweetness, playfulness and charm. Vishnupriya caressed His lotus feet; full of rasa, He was the crown of the kings of rasikas3.

Verse 5

विद्याविलासेन विलोलबाहु-
र्गच्छन्पथि शिष्यसमाकुलो हरिः।
आगत्य गेहे निजमातुरन्तिके
तस्याः सुखं नित्यमधात्प्रियासमम्॥५॥

vidyāvilāsena vilolabāhu-
rgacchanpathi śiṣyasamākulo hariḥ|
āgatya gehe nijamāturantike
tasyāḥ sukhaṁ nityamadhātpriyāsamam||5||

vidya-vilasena — in the play of learning; vilola-bahuh — swinging His arms; gachchhan — walking; pathi — on the road; shishya-samakulah — thronged by students; harih — Hari; agatya — coming; gehe — home; nija-matuh — of His mother; antike — into the presence; tasyah — to her; sukham — joy; nityam — always; adhat — gave; priya-samam — equally with His beloved.

5Rapt in the play of learning, Hari walked along the road swinging His arms, thronged by His students; and coming home to His mother, He always gave her joy equally with His beloved wife.

Verse 6

ततः स लोकाननुशिक्षयन्मन-
श्चकार कर्तुं पितृकार्यमच्युतः।
श्राद्धं स कृत्वा विधिवद्विधानवि-
द्गयां प्रतस्थे क्षितिदेवतान्वितः॥६॥

tataḥ sa lokānanuśikṣayanmana-
ścakāra kartuṁ pitṛkāryamacyutaḥ|
śrāddhaṁ sa kṛtvā vidhivadvidhānavi-
dgayāṁ pratasthe kṣitidevatānvitaḥ||6||

tatah — then; sah — He; lokan — people; anushikshayan — teaching; manah chakara — resolved; kartum — to perform; pitri-karyam — the rite for His father; achyutah — Achyuta; shraddham — the shraddha; sah — He; kritva — performing; vidhivat — duly; vidhana-vit — knower of the injunctions; gayam — for Gaya; pratasthe — set out; kshiti-devata-anvitah — accompanied by the gods on earth (brahmanas).

6Then Achyuta, teaching people, resolved to perform the rite for His father. Knower of the injunctions, He duly performed the shraddha and set out for Gaya with the gods on earth4.

Verse 7

गच्छन्पथि प्राकृतचेष्टया हस-
न्नर्मोक्तिभिः कौतुकमावहन्सताम्।
रेमे कुरङ्गावलिराजितासु
स्थलीषु पश्यन्मृगकौतुकानि॥७॥

gacchanpathi prākṛtaceṣṭayā hasa-
nnarmoktibhiḥ kautukamāvahansatām|
reme kuraṅgāvalirājitāsu
sthalīṣu paśyanmṛgakautukāni||7||

gachchhan — going; pathi — along the road; prakrita-cheshtaya — with the manners of an ordinary man; hasan — laughing; narma-uktibhih — with jests; kautukam — merriment; avahan — bringing; satam — to the good; reme — He delighted; kuranga-avali-rajitasu — graced by herds of antelope; sthalishu — on the plains; pashyan — watching; mriga-kautukani — the frolics of the animals.

7Going along the road, He behaved like an ordinary man: He laughed and amused the good with His jests, and on the plains graced by herds of antelope He delighted in watching the frolics of the animals.

Verse 8

स्नात्वा स चोरान्धयके नदे मुदा
कृत्वाह्निकं देवपितॄन्यथाविधि।
सन्तर्पयित्वा सहसान्वितः प्रियै-
र्मन्दारमारुह्य ददर्श देवताः॥८॥

snātvā sa corāndhayake nade mudā
kṛtvāhnikaṁ devapitṝnyathāvidhi|
santarpayitvā sahasānvitaḥ priyai-
rmandāramāruhya dadarśa devatāḥ||8||

snatva — bathing; sah — He; chorandhayake nade — in the river Chorandhayaka; muda — joyfully; kritva — performing; ahnikam — the daily rites; deva-pitrin — the gods and forefathers; yatha-vidhi — according to the rules; santarpayitva — satisfying (with libations); sahasa — then at once; anvitah priyaih — with His dear companions; mandaram — Mandara; aruhya — climbing; dadarsha — saw; devatah — the Deities.

8Having joyfully bathed in the river Chorandhayaka and performed His daily rites according to the rules, He satisfied the gods and forefathers with libations, and then, with His dear companions, climbed Mount Mandara and saw the Deities there5.

Verse 9

ततोऽवतीर्यावजगाम सत्वरं
धराधराधो भवनं द्विजस्य सः।
मनुष्यशिक्षामनुदर्शयन्प्रभु-
र्ज्वरेण सन्तप्ततनुर्बभूव॥९॥

tato'vatīryāvajagāma satvaraṁ
dharādharādho bhavanaṁ dvijasya saḥ|
manuṣyaśikṣāmanudarśayanprabhu-
rjvareṇa santaptatanurbabhūva||9||

tatah — then; avatirya — descending; avajagama — went down; satvaram — quickly; dharadhara-adhah — at the foot of the mountain; bhavanam — to the house; dvijasya — of a brahmana; sah — He; manushya-shiksham — a lesson for men; anudarshayan — showing; prabhuh — Prabhu; jvarena — with fever; santapta-tanuh — His body burning; babhuva — became.

9Then Prabhu quickly came down to the house of a brahmana at the foot of the mountain; and, giving a lesson to people, He fell ill with a burning fever.

Verse 10

बभूव मे वर्त्मनि दैवयोगा-
च्छरीरवैवश्यमतः कथं स्यात्।
गयासु मे पैतृककर्मविघ्नः
श्रेयस्यभूदित्यतिचिन्तयाकुलः॥१०॥

babhūva me vartmani daivayogā-
ccharīravaivaśyamataḥ kathaṁ syāt|
gayāsu me paitṛkakarmavighnaḥ
śreyasyabhūdityaticintayākulaḥ||10||

babhuva — has come; me — upon Me; vartmani — on the way; daiva-yogat — by the will of fate; sharira-vaivashyam — weakness of body; atah — so; katham — how; syat — will (it) be (done); gayasu — at Gaya; me — My; paitrika-karma-vighnah — an obstacle to the rite for My father; shreyasi — in a good (work); abhut — has arisen; iti — thus; ati-chintaya — with great anxiety; akulah — troubled.

10"On the way, by the will of fate, My body has grown weak," He thought anxiously. "How now will My rite for My father be performed at Gaya? An obstacle has arisen to a good work."

Verse 11

ततोऽप्युपायं परिचिन्तयन्स्वयं
ज्वरस्य शान्त्यै द्विजपादसेवनम्।
वरं स विज्ञाय तथोपपादयं-
स्तदम्बुपानं भगवांश्चकार॥११॥

tato'pyupāyaṁ paricintayansvayaṁ
jvarasya śāntyai dvijapādasevanam|
varaṁ sa vijñāya tathopapādayaṁ-
stadambupānaṁ bhagavāṁścakāra||11||

tatah — then; api — indeed; upayam — a remedy; parichintayan — considering; svayam — Himself; jvarasya — of the fever; shantyai — for the cure; dvija-pada-sevanam — service to the feet of brahmanas; varam — the best; sah — He; vijnaya — recognising; tatha — so; upapadayan — arranging; tat-ambu-panam — drinking of that water (from their feet); bhagavan — Bhagavan; chakara — did.

11Then, considering a remedy for the fever Himself, He recognised the service of brahmanas' feet as the best of all, and, arranging it so, Bhagavan drank the water that had washed their feet.

Verse 12

ये सर्वविप्रा मधुसूदनाश्रया
निरन्तरं कृष्णपदाभिचिन्तकाः।
ततः स्वयं कृष्णजनाभिमानी
तेषां परं पादजलं पपौ प्रभुः॥१२॥

ye sarvaviprā madhusūdanāśrayā
nirantaraṁ kṛṣṇapadābhicintakāḥ|
tataḥ svayaṁ kṛṣṇajanābhimānī
teṣāṁ paraṁ pādajalaṁ papau prabhuḥ||12||

ye — who; sarva-viprah — all the brahmanas; madhusudana-ashrayah — sheltered in Madhusudana; nirantaram — ceaselessly; krishna-pada-abhichintakah — meditating on Krishna's feet; tatah — therefore; svayam — Himself; krishna-jana-abhimani — regarding Himself as one of Krishna's people; tesham — their; param — only; pada-jalam — foot-water; papau — drank; prabhuh — Prabhu.

12All those brahmanas had taken shelter in Madhusudana and ceaselessly meditated on Krishna's feet. That is why Prabhu, who regarded Himself as one of Krishna's people, drank the water from their feet.

Verse 13

ततो ज्वरस्योपशमो बभूव
तान्दर्शयित्वा द्विजपादभक्तिम्।
जगाम तीर्थं स पुनःपुनाख्यं
चकार तत्र द्विजदेवतार्चनम्॥१३॥

tato jvarasyopaśamo babhūva
tāndarśayitvā dvijapādabhaktim|
jagāma tīrthaṁ sa punaḥpunākhyaṁ
cakāra tatra dvijadevatārcanam||13||

tatah — then; jvarasya — of the fever; upashamah — abatement; babhuva — came; tan — to them; darshayitva — showing; dvija-pada-bhaktim — devotion to the feet of brahmanas; jagama — went; tirtham — to the holy place; sah — He; punahpuna-akhyam — called Punahpuna; chakara — performed; tatra — there; dvija-devata-archanam — worship of brahmanas and gods.

13And the fever abated. Having shown them what devotion to the feet of brahmanas is, He went to the holy place called Punahpuna6 and there worshipped the brahmanas and the gods.

Verse 14

ततः समुत्तीर्य नदीं स गच्छं-
स्तीर्थोत्तमे राजगृहे सुपुण्ये।
ब्रह्माख्यकुण्डे पितृदेवपूजां
चकार लोकाननुशिक्षयन्सः॥१४॥

tataḥ samuttīrya nadīṁ sa gacchaṁ-
stīrthottame rājagṛhe supuṇye|
brahmākhyakuṇḍe pitṛdevapūjāṁ
cakāra lokānanuśikṣayansaḥ||14||

tatah — then; samuttirya — crossing; nadim — the river; sah — He; gachchhan — going on; tirtha-uttame — in the best of holy places; rajagrihe — at Rajagriha; su-punye — most sacred; brahma-akhya-kunde — at the pond called Brahma(-kunda); pitri-deva-pujam — worship of forefathers and gods; chakara — performed; lokan — people; anushikshayan — teaching; sah — He.

14Crossing the river and going on, He, teaching people, worshipped the forefathers and the gods at the pond called Brahma-kunda in Rajagriha7, the most sacred of holy places.

Verse 15

पत्या स्वमातुः ससुरोऽगमच्छनै-
र्गयां गदाभृच्चरणं दिदृक्षुः॥१५॥

patyā svamātuḥ sasuro'gamacchanai-
rgayāṁ gadābhṛccaraṇaṁ didṛkṣuḥ||15||

patya — with (for the sake of) the husband; sva-matuh — of His mother; sa-surah — with the (earthly) gods; agamat — came; shanaih — slowly; gayam — to Gaya; gada-bhrit-charanam — the feet of the Club-bearer; didrikshuh — wishing to see.

15…For the sake of His mother's husband8 He came slowly, with the gods on earth, to Gaya, wishing to see the feet of the Club-bearer9.

Verse 16

तस्मिन्शुभं न्यासिवरं ददर्श
स ईश्वराख्यं हरिपादभक्तम्।
पुरीं परेशः परयात्मभक्त्या
तुष्टं ननामैनमथाब्रवीच्च॥१६॥

tasminśubhaṁ nyāsivaraṁ dadarśa
sa īśvarākhyaṁ haripādabhaktam|
purīṁ pareśaḥ parayātmabhaktyā
tuṣṭaṁ nanāmainamathābravīcca||16||

tasmin — there; shubham — auspicious; nyasi-varam — the best of sannyasis; dadarsha — saw; sah — He; ishvara-akhyam — named Ishvara; hari-pada-bhaktam — devoted to Hari's feet; purim — Puri; para-ishah — the Supreme Lord; paraya — with supreme; atma-bhaktya — heartfelt devotion; tushtam — pleased; nanama — bowed; enam — to him; atha — then; abravit — spoke; cha — and.

16There the Supreme Lord saw the auspicious Ishvara Puri, the best of sannyasis, devoted to Hari's feet. With the deepest devotion of His heart He bowed to him, and he was pleased. Then the Lord said:

Verse 17

दिष्ट्याद्य दृष्टं भगवन्पदाम्बुजं
तव प्रभो ब्रूहि यथा भवाम्बुधिम्।
निस्तीर्य कृष्णाङ्घ्रिसरोरुहामृतं
पश्यामि तन्मे करुणानिधे स्वयम्॥१७॥

diṣṭyādya dṛṣṭaṁ bhagavanpadāmbujaṁ
tava prabho brūhi yathā bhavāmbudhim|
nistīrya kṛṣṇāṅghrisaroruhāmṛtaṁ
paśyāmi tanme karuṇānidhe svayam||17||

dishtya — by good fortune; adya — today; drishtam — are seen; bhagavan — O revered one; pada-ambujam — the lotus feet; tava — your; prabho — O master; bruhi — tell; yatha — how; bhava-ambudhim — the ocean of worldly existence; nistirya — crossing; krishna-anghri-saroruha-amritam — the nectar of Krishna's lotus feet; pashyami — I may behold (taste); tat — that; me — to me; karuna-nidhe — O treasury of mercy; svayam — yourself.

17"O revered one! By good fortune I have seen your lotus feet today. Tell Me yourself, O master, O treasury of mercy, how I may cross the ocean of worldly existence and taste the nectar of Krishna's lotus feet."10

Verse 18

स इत्थमाकर्ण्य हरेर्वचोऽमृतं
मुदा ददौ मन्त्रवरं मतिज्ञः।
दशाक्षरं प्राप्य स गौरचन्द्रमा-
स्तुष्टाव तं भक्तिविभावितः स्वयम्॥१८॥

sa itthamākarṇya harervaco'mṛtaṁ
mudā dadau mantravaraṁ matijñaḥ|
daśākṣaraṁ prāpya sa gauracandramā-
stuṣṭāva taṁ bhaktivibhāvitaḥ svayam||18||

sah — he; ittham — thus; akarnya — hearing; hareh — of Hari; vachah-amritam — the nectar of words; muda — gladly; dadau — gave; mantra-varam — the best of mantras; mati-jnah — knowing (His) heart; dasha-aksharam — the ten-syllable (mantra); prapya — receiving; sah — He; gaura-chandramah — Gaurachandra; tushtava — praised; tam — him; bhakti-vibhavitah — overwhelmed by devotion; svayam — Himself.

18Hearing these nectarean words of Hari, Puri, who knew His heart, gladly gave Him the best of mantras — the ten-syllable one11. Having received it, Gaurachandra Himself, overwhelmed by devotion, praised him:

Verse 19

न्यासिन्दयालो तव पादसङ्गमा-
त्कृतार्थता मेऽद्य बभूव दुर्लभा।
श्रीकृष्णपादाब्जमधून्मदा च सा
यथा तरिष्यामि दुरन्तसंसृतिम्॥१९॥

nyāsindayālo tava pādasaṅgamā-
tkṛtārthatā me'dya babhūva durlabhā|
śrīkṛṣṇapādābjamadhūnmadā ca sā
yathā tariṣyāmi durantasaṁsṛtim||19||

nyasin — O sannyasi; dayalo — O merciful one; tava — your; pada-sangamat — from contact with the feet; krita-arthata — fulfilment; me — my; adya — today; babhuva — has come; durlabha — rare; shri-krishna-pada-abja-madhu-unmada — intoxicated with the honey of Sri Krishna's lotus feet; cha — and; sa — that; yatha — so that; tarishyami — I shall cross; duranta-samsritim — the endless round of birth and death.

19"O sannyasi, O merciful one! Through contact with your feet I have today attained a rare fulfilment — intoxication with the honey of Sri Krishna's lotus feet, by which I shall cross the endless round of birth and death."

Thus ends the fifteenth sarga, "The Meeting with Srimad Ishvara Puri" (Shrimad-ishvara-puri-darshana), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Vaidyas: the community of physicians, to which Murari Gupta himself belonged.
  2. Vachaspati is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods and the model of eloquence; Kavya is Shukra, the preceptor of the asuras and the model of the poet. The sense: their eloquence and poetry, and the moon's radiance, belong originally to the Lord, and when He came to earth they gave Him back, as it were, what had been deposited with them.
  3. Rasa is the taste, the inner experience of loving service; rasikas are those able to relish it.
  4. That is, with brahmanas.
  5. Mandara is a sacred hill in Bihar (near present-day Bhagalpur), where Madhusudana is worshipped.
  6. Punahpuna (the present Punpun) is a sacred river on the way to Gaya.
  7. Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir) is an ancient holy town in Bihar.
  8. In all witnesses only half of this verse survives. Literally "with His mother's husband," that is, apparently, for the sake of His late father, Jagannatha Mishra; the sense is conjectural.
  9. The Club-bearer is Gadadhara, Vishnu as worshipped at Gaya; His footprint (Vishnu-pada) is the chief shrine of Gaya.
  10. The Lord speaks as a seeking disciple, setting an example for people (cf. vv. 6, 9, 13): this is how one should approach a guru. He Himself is never subject to the round of birth and death (cf. v. 19).
  11. The ten-syllable mantra is the mantra of Gopala-Krishna.
